usageNotes: Use this to enable/disable the cluster-wide firewall or change its default policies and logging behavior. Changes take effect immediately across all nodes without a task UPID — the response is null on success. Pass the `digest` from `get_cluster_firewall_options` to guard against concurrent modifications; omit it only when you are certain no concurrent edits are possible.

examples.summary: Enable the cluster firewall with DROP default input policy and rate-limited logging

tips: The firewall is disabled by default (enable=0); enabling it cluster-wide will enforce policy_in/policy_out on all nodes immediately — verify your rules before setting policy_in to DROP or REJECT to avoid locking yourself out.
Use the `delete` param (comma-separated config key names) to revert specific settings back to their defaults rather than overwriting with explicit values.

ebtables controls layer-2 (Ethernet bridge) filtering; leave it enabled (default) unless you have a specific reason to disable it, as disabling it removes bridge-level MAC/ARP filtering across the cluster.
Fetch the current digest via GET /cluster/firewall/options and echo it back to prevent a lost-update race condition in automation scripts.
